A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same universal image-immunization work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original immunization experiments, transferability and robustness evaluations, ablations, and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator results and controlled qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: The target semantic injection and source semantic suppression losses, universal perturbation optimization, data-free variant and additive inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move to the appendix; expanded explanations and new evaluations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-Edit, MagicBrush instruction-edit pairs and DiffusionGuard's real-image inpainting benchmark, extending v1's synthetic evaluation and COCO/DomainNet coverage. Noun-free and null-prompt evaluations introduce distinct text-conditioning scenarios. Inpainting and diffusion-transformer evaluation themselves already existed in v1.

E2.justification: FastProtect joins retained editing comparisons, and DiffVax joins the original inpainting comparison. Complex-prompt and purification comparisons gain image-specific and optimization-free comparators. EditShield disappears from the original white-box and training-size comparisons, while its SD1.4/2.0 transfer results are retained elsewhere and a MagicBrush comparison is added.

E3.justification: Core training and diffusion settings remain stable. V2 removes DINO similarity, replaces AHIQ with LPIPS for imperceptibility, and introduces FastProtect budget calibration at 22/255 and CPU timing. The retained SD1.5 inpainting evaluation is described as black-box for Ours rather than white-box; unchanged scores do not establish that it was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds null-prompt mechanism controls, noun-free prompt tests and qualitative budget tests at 2/255–6/255, while expanding complex-prompt and purification analyses. GrIDPure replaces AdverseCleaner. Conversely, v1's checkerboard-target study and 16/255 black-box comparison disappear. Training-size, loss-component, ImageNet-Excluded and convergence analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions state averaging over 10 random seeds and retain the same plus/minus reporting and across-target mean/standard-deviation practice. New result rows do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run count or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark and comparator results while removing DINO and several ablation entries. Retained universal scores are mostly unchanged, but Table 4's Ours CLIP similarity changes from 0.670 to 0.673. Table 3's JPEG LPIPS changes from 0.419 to 0.511 without an explained cause, so this is not an established same-setting gain. New MagicBrush results favor EditShield over Ours on LPIPS, 0.588 versus 0.568.

T1.justification: The objectives, cross-attention equations, residual update and attention-map invariance argument are mathematically retained. V1 Section 4.4 becomes v2 Appendix A.5 with revised explanation, without a new proof, derivation or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a single universal perturbation, two semantic losses and a data-free variant. V2 extends its principal comparative claims to optimization-free methods and explicitly claims a favorable performance–latency–memory trade-off against these alternatives.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of prompt-independent semantic injection, attribute-level target transfer and category-independent suppression using the retained ImageNet-Excluded results. It qualifies semantic transfer to DiT models, discusses EditShield's instruction-editing advantage, and expands discussion of mask sensitivity and purification robustness.

D1.justification: V2 documents FastProtect calibration, GPT-4 prompt elaboration and the existing ImageNet-Excluded experiment's 136-class exclusion and 10,000-image sampling. It adds a project-page URL but removes v1's explicit code/data/seeds release statement and inpainting perturbation-budget disclosure. Actual external resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work relative to optimization-free defenses, especially FastProtect and DiffVax, rather than principally per-image optimization. Related work also expands to purification-resistant methods such as BlurGuard, DCT-Shield and AntiPure, alongside additional editing defenses.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Theory and pseudocode move to the appendix, empirical discussion is reordered, and previously isolated appendix tables receive dedicated explanatory subsections. These changes substantially reorganize the document beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 1 with three defense categories and a latency/performance/memory plot, separates the framework illustration, adds mechanism and real-image figures, and restructures numerous tables. Typography and page layout change throughout. Appendix figure/table numbering now overlaps some main-text numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important evidentiary gaps: FastProtect/DiffVax comparisons directly test the central efficiency claim, new real-image benchmarks extend the existing COCO/DomainNet validation, and null-prompt controls provide stronger evidence for semantic injection. These gains substantially improve the paper despite narrower retained metric/ablation coverage, unexplained JPEG-score revisions and some numbering ambiguity.
